 Cognizant Cognizant wins £133.2m Network Rail tech contract.
 Beats rivals TCS, HCLTech, DXC, and Atos for the deal.
 Seven-year agreement covers data centre and cloud ops.
 Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery
 Webinar by Vishal Malkan

 in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan
 Register for FREE Webinar Register for FREE 
 IT services major Cognizant has emerged as the winner of a £133.2-million (approximately $175 million) technology infrastructure contract from the UK's Network Rail Infrastructure Limited, beating four competitors, including Indian IT majors Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and HCLTech.
 The nearly seven-year contract covers the management and operation of Network Rail's data centre infrastructure, including networks, servers, mainframes, cloud platforms, and associated IT services, according to a contract award notice published on a UK government's portal on November 12.
 Besides TCS and HCLTech, global technology services companies DXC Technology and Atos IT Services UK were among the unsuccessful bidders.
 The procurement attracted five bids, all of which were assessed in the final stage, with Cognizant emerging as the sole successful supplier.
 The contract is valued at £133.2 million excluding value-added tax (VAT), rising to £159.84 million including VAT.

 Jobs for locals: Pro-Kannada activists visit Bengaluru IT firms to collect employment data despite C... 
 Beyond the Nasdaq: How AI reset will impact domestic IT stocks 
 The Network Rail contract adds to Cognizant's recent large deal wins amid a challenging demand environment for IT services companies. The seven-year engagement provides long-term revenue visibility and highlights the importance of infrastructure management deals in sustaining growth.
 On July 21, 2026, Moneycontrol exclusively reported that Cognizant had secured a mega deal potentially worth over $500 million from US healthcare company Centene, an existing client, with the contract likely comprising a mix of renewals and new business.
 Emails sent to Cognizant, TCS, HCLTech, DXC Technology, and Atos seeking comments did not elicit an immediate response.
 Key Takeaways
 £133.2 million Contract Value Cognizant won a £133.2-million technology infrastructure contract from the UK's Network Rail Infrastructure Limited, rising to £159.84 million including VAT. 
 7 years Contract Duration The nearly seven-year contract covers the management and operation of Network Rail's data centre infrastructure, set to begin in 2027. 
 5 Total Bids The procurement attracted five bids, including Indian IT majors Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and HCLTech, alongside DXC Technology and Atos IT Services UK. 
 COMPETITIVE WIN Cognizant emerged as the sole successful supplier, beating four competitors in a competitive flexible procedure under the UK's Procurement Act 2023. 
 What the contract covers 
 Under the agreement, Cognizant will provide data centre infrastructure services to support Network Rail's technology operations across physical data centres, local area network (LAN) and edge computing rooms, and cloud platforms.
 The scope includes local and wide area networks (LAN and WAN), mainframes, servers, technology platforms, specified applications, and the tools and services required to operate the infrastructure.
 Network Rail sought a single technology partner to manage these services, consolidating responsibility for a broad range of infrastructure operations under one contract.
 The contract also includes provisions for optional project services, allowing Network Rail to procure additional services during the agreement's validity.
 Seven-year contract to begin in 2027 
 Network Rail made the award decision on November 11, 2026, following a competitive procurement process under the UK's Procurement Act 2023.
 However, the contract has not yet been formally signed.
 The procurement is currently subject to a standstill period ending November 23, during which unsuccessful bidders have an opportunity to review the award decision before the contract proceeds.
 The agreement represents a long-term infrastructure services engagement for Cognizant in the UK, with the company set to assume responsibility for multiple components of Network Rail's technology infrastructure.
 Competitive win against Indian IT rivals 
 The contract award comes amid competition among global IT services companies for large, multi-year infrastructure management deals.
 For Cognizant, the selection marks a competitive win against TCS and HCLTech, two of India's largest IT services companies, alongside international competitors DXC Technology and Atos.
 The procurement followed a competitive flexible procedure, with all five bidders reaching the final assessment stage.
 An earlier tender notice had placed the estimated procurement value at £185.3 million, compared with the final award value of £133.2 million. However, the published award notice does not explain the difference or disclose the individual financial bids submitted by the unsuccessful companies.
 The contract adds to Cognizant's portfolio of large infrastructure services engagements, giving the company a long-term role in supporting the technology systems of one of Britain's major railway infrastructure organisations.
